claims.text: CALPHAD can be used to assess phase stability in high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD can be used for microstructure refinement in high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD can be used for property optimization in high-entropy alloys.
Thermal analysis and microstructural characterization can be used to investigate phase transitions and microstructural evolution in high-entropy alloys.
High-entropy alloys can exhibit phase transitions.
High-entropy alloys can undergo microstructural evolution during thermal processing.
The phases present in high-entropy alloys influence their properties.
CALPHAD models thermodynamic properties and phase transitions.
Modeling thermodynamic properties and phase transitions with CALPHAD enables prediction of phase stability.
Modeling thermodynamic properties and phase transitions with CALPHAD enables prediction of microstructure refinement.
Modeling thermodynamic properties and phase transitions with CALPHAD enables property optimization.
Applying CALPHAD improves phase stability in high-entropy alloys.
Applying CALPHAD produces a refined microstructure in high-entropy alloys.
Applying CALPHAD produces optimized properties in high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD requires further assessment to determine transition temperatures for intermetallic formation.
The complexity of high-entropy alloys and limitations of CALPHAD create uncertainty in phase-stability and microstructure predictions.

contradictions.description: The mechanism describes CALPHAD as a predictive modeling framework, but the intervention, baseline, outcome, and experiment treat its application as a physical treatment that directly improves phase stability and refines the alloy. Prediction or design guidance does not by itself alter a material without a specified composition or processing change.
